title: Turn-scoped metadata falls back to updating an unrelated message
reasoning: When a metadata event includes a turnRef, updateLastMessageBySender first looks for a same-turn message, but if none is found it falls back to the last message from that sender without any turnRef. The metadata handlers pass turnRefForUpdate(event), so an out-of-order, replayed, or delayed metadata event for a missing turn can overwrite systemPrompt, fullUserMessage, or tool schema data on a different user message. That corrupts the transcript context displayed and persisted for the wrong turn instead of dropping or buffering unmatched metadata.
recommendation: When a turnRef is supplied, only update a message whose turnRef matches. If unmatched metadata must be tolerated, buffer it by turnRef or log/drop it; reserve sender-only fallback for events that truly have no turnRef.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests, and no included test evidence exercises out-of-order or unmatched turnRef metadata events.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a frontend hook/store test that creates a previous user message with turnRef A, then sends user_message_metadata or tool_schemas_metadata with turnRef B and asserts the turnRef A message is not modified.
minimumFixScope: Change useStreamMessageUpdaters.updateLastMessageBySender so the sender-only fallback is not used when a non-empty turnRef is provided, then cover the metadata handlers that rely on it.
